fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the single access point at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach all structures without obstruction.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the end of the access drive so fire apparatus and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to maintain overhead and side clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive so responders on foot can move alongside vehicles safely.
• Thin vegetation growing close to the exterior walls of all structures so responders can move around each building without obstruction.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the access drive, and the storage area.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and both detached structures so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Keep the storage area accessible and clearly identified so responders know its location and can avoid mistaking it for a habitable structure.
• Trim any vegetation that blocks sight lines between the street and the structures so arriving responders can see the buildings from the access point.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris visible near the structures before fire season.
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim overhanging branches and shrubs that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure walls.
• Cut grass around the structures short and keep it mowed through the dry season.
• Clear shrubs and low branches along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim tree branches that hang over the driveway to keep the full width and height of the travel lane open.
• Separate shrub groupings near the structures so there is bare ground or mowed grass between each plant and the building.
• Remove scattered shrubs that sit between the tree cluster and the structure to break up the connection between them.
• Thin scattered trees near the structures so individual tree canopies are not touching each other.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, debris, and low-hanging vegetation at all times.
• Move any stored wood, lumber, or other woody material away from the exterior walls of the structures.
• Mow or cut grass along both sides of the driveway to reduce the amount of dry grass that could carry fire toward the structure.
